items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: And, uh, Martha Boswell and, and, and Connie and, and, uh, that. Used to have a little, they used to have a little trio. And I used to go, they lived on, down here on Camp Street and used to go by their house and play.

ctx.x: I was gonna ask first of all, just how old you were when you started with the drums? Had you played anything else at all first? That was a very good thing.

No, no, that was, that was, on account of my dad being there. Yeah. He bought me, first he bought me a snare drum. You see? Mm-hmm. And then I just, just played the snare drum. Like I told you, every time they'd come running for Rag Baby, well I'd have to take his place. And then, and then the parades. You had your own snare drum then you got. My dad bought me a snare drum. Incidentally, later on he hocked it. And, and I went to, there was a place down here on, down around Napoleon Avenue called the Mysterious…
Well, they didn't live across the river then. No. Well, I thought maybe they were from over there. They never did live across, no, the Hardys lived across the river, you see.
